params.place: on the map: North Africa, the Sahara

moments.what: the Sahara's countries glow sand-gold, SAHARA writes across them
the sand flickers green
grass covers it for a moment, a hippo standing in the middle
the green fades back to sand, the camera closes in
a green sprout pushes up from the sand

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The Sahara used to be green grassland. So could it really turn green again?

params.place: on the map: the Sahara under a flipping counter

moments.what: dunes ripple across the whole Sahara
a counter board stands up on the Libyan sand
the counter flips up to the figure
the camera pulls back over all of Africa
the land goes sand-gold
the counter board rattles
it washes green
and back to sand again

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The biggest hot desert on Earth already has, more than 230 times in the last eight million years, flipping from desert to green and back again.

params.place: on the map: a globe over the Mediterranean, rain bands over the Sahel

moments.what: a small globe rises over the Mediterranean
its axis traces a slow circle
the axis line starts its circle
the axis line glows
the globe leans over toward the sun
a sun swings round and its rays hit the globe
the rays land on North Africa on the map
rain clouds gather over the Gulf of Guinea
rain starts to fall from the clouds
the rain band slides north
the clouds reach the middle of the desert
rain falls on the dunes, dark patches spread

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So what flips it? Earth wobbles slowly on its axis, and when the wobble tilts more summer sun onto North Africa, the monsoon rains push north, deep into the sand.

params.place: on the map: the green Sahara, a great lake at Chad

moments.what: the camera glides south over the desert
green paints across from the south
dune marks fade under it
a huge lake fills at Chad
a hippo pops up in the lake
a crocodile slides along the shore
a giraffe stands up on the grass
a camel ghosts in, the animals fade to it
the camel plods on, dunes return

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Last time, grass covered the dunes and lakes filled the basins. Hippos, crocodiles and giraffes lived right where camels walk across the sand today.

params.place: on the map: Tassili in Algeria, a painted rock face

moments.what: small herders walk across the green
a herd of cattle follows them
a hand-painted cow outline appears
the camera pushes in on a red rock face standing in southern Algeria
more painted cattle appear on the rock
Algeria outlines itself and its name writes on

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: People herded cattle across it, and painted them on rocks still standing in the Algerian desert today.

params.place: on the map: the Sahara, the Atlantic, the Amazon

moments.what: the map snaps back to sand
wind lines sweep west off the coast
an orange dust plume lifts off the desert
the camera pulls back as the plume crosses the ocean
the plume stretches on over open water
Brazil's rainforest lights up green where the plume lands
dust specks sink into the trees
small trees sprout taller

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But here's the catch. Every year the wind carries Sahara dust across the Atlantic Ocean, thousands of kilometres, all the way to the Amazon rainforest, and that dust feeds its soil.

params.place: on the map: the plume thinning over the Atlantic

moments.what: green sweeps over the Sahara
the plume's source dims
the dust plume thins and breaks
dust settles back onto the green Sahara
the camera glides west to the Amazon
the trees there sway
a dashed line measures the ocean between them
a fertiliser sack on the forest edge empties
the sack tips over, a red arrow drops

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Turn the Sahara green, and much of that dust stays put on the ground. The world's biggest rainforest, half a world away, would lose one of its fertilisers.

params.place: on the map: Africa under a turning wheel of years

moments.what: a big dial board rises over the Mediterranean
the globe's axis circles on the dial
the dial's hand sweeps round
the figure stamps on the dial
the camera starts to pull back over Africa
rain clouds drift north again
green pulses up from the south
the dial hand keeps turning
the Sahara washes green

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And here's the twist: the wobble comes round about every 21,000 years, so scientists expect the rains to return one day, thousands of years from now.

params.place: on the map: Africa and Antarctica, then the Sahara again

moments.what: a pin glows on the Sahara
a pin glows on Antarctica
a question mark hops between them
a comment bubble pops up
its words write on
the camera dives back to the Sahara: the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Green Sahara or melted Antarctica: which what-if should we map next? Tell me in the comments below. And now picture it one more time:
